segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: We are going to talk in all Cherokee for a little while. I am just going to ask y’all what is written. If you don’t like something that I am asking you, it is going to be this one’s fault.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That is how he treats me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Y’all can get on to her. First thing, what are your names in English and Cherokee?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Levi Eagle is my name. They call me Tsigila in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Tsigila, yeah, who gave you the name Tsigila?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: I don’t remember. They gave me a nickname when I would pour drinks. I was putting drink into jugs. They gave me the name Jug for a nickname.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What about you? The same thing?

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: Johnny Lee Soap. Atsilidosgi is my name in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Who gave you the name Atsilidosgi? The name that you have?

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: I would say my mother.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: The same for me, too.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: Just as a nickname, my family call me Jugasdani.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, OK.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: That is how the whites say it, too. They call it a given name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, Richard is my real name, but they call me Guy in Cherokee and in English. I don’t know who gave me that name either.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: I guess it was our mom who named us. All our family that are there have Cherokee names. Some might not even know.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really, a long time ago. They gave a Cherokee name they would get from a long time ago, when the elders were alive, so it wouldn’t fade away.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: Like for instance, they would give their grandmother’s name and nowadays it’s all different.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, it’s all different now, it’s true.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: I wonder whose name was Tsigili? I wonder how they found that, I wonder. Tsigili - I have only seen one with the same name. I told him, “You have a beautiful name.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where were you born when y’all came into this world?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Sequoyah County, both of us.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Sequoyah County.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Both of us.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: You could say here.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Hastings.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Just at Hastings.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: And then, just here where we grew up, just where we live, we still live where we were raised.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, has it completely changed since you were growing up?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: It has changed.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: Everything changes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Amen.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: Even children will not come visit you nowadays. This one that’s with me is the only one that comes to visit me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: There are four of them. Five in all, or four - I lost one boy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: But they come around only when they want something.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: That is what I was telling him.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: It’s true. That is the way it is.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: If they want something, they come back, I was telling him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: But you wouldn’t think about it, you would help them. Yeah.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: If they ask you for something, you feel sorry for them and must do it for them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: When y’all were growing up, what did y’all have to play with? Were y’all ball players, or what?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Baseball.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Baseball.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: I played both baseball and softball.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Softball. Were you the pitcher?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: No, I was the back catcher.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, really.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: He was the pitcher.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: I just played baseball. Softball is for women to play. They asked me one time, when baseball changed into softball, “Would you help us?” they said. I said, “No, I don’t want to play with a softball. It is for women to play.”

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: And we didn’t play basketball when I was in school. There was just one goal, that was why we didn’t play that basketball.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: And nowadays, it’s a going thing.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Boy, that’s true.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: They really like it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Some are making big money.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Big.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Just playing ball.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: Those big pros, they are getting paid big. I bet they are as tall as this is [gestures].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, some are that tall.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: So are those women that play. They are big, too.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Very true.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, true it is. As for me, I didn’t know that we had it hard growing up. There would be food on the table when she cooked. You wouldn’t think there was hardly anything, but the table would be full when it came time to eat. Did y’all grow up the same way, or didn’t you?

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: We grew up hard.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: We grew up hard with what we went through, but it didn’t seem hard for me. My late grandmother had an oil well in Tulsa. She would feed us. She would have money in her pockets. She would get a lot of money back then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: She was feeding two houses.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I’ll be.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: She would live at one for a little while, and then another. She would just do that, and then when she passed, it was then we had it a little harder.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: As for me, it was all the time. We had it hard all time. Our late mother - there wasn’t money coming from anywhere. It was hard to find work. She would just make things. She had one of those things they call a kettle. She would build a fire there, and make soap herself to wash our clothes. That is what she did.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: I was just six years old when our dad passed. He has a different dad.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, OK.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That was when our mother really saw it hard. Our dad had almost 500 acres. He was a big farmer. He was doing good, and then when he passed, it went down. Our mom was not able to do it by herself, to feed us and pay all the tax so she lost almost all of it. It’s true our mother went through some hard times feeding that many children. She was probably getting just a little bit old.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And my late mother, we would just sometimes eat water gravy. I don’t know if y’all may have eaten like that.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: It was the same for me growing up, but there was Mom getting our food. She would cook for us three times a day.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah that is what I was saying.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That is the way it was. It was hard, but the family would eat. They would prepare something to eat three times a day.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They would cook in the morning and at noon, and in the evening they would prepare. Yes, I think about that sometimes. We were not really starving, I think. Sometimes we would just have bread and water gravy, and we would be full.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I still like it, water gravy.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: I remember a long time ago, they would get stamps and get food. It was just measured, telling you what you could get. It was really hard back then. They would go around borrowing those stamps when they wanted coffee. To get coffee, they would be asking for stamps. You couldn’t get anything back then unless you had a stamp.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Y’all really did come through hard times, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Yes, I remember. I was telling the ones that are growing up how we grew up and how we ate. We ate birds, squirrels, and rabbits. Those little snowbirds like that [gestures], they would make dumplings, and I guess God fed those squalisda, those blackbirds. Lots of them would come, and they would not go to the woods. They would group up around houses, and we would kill them there. Nobody had a gun, and I don’t know if you have seen those what do they call them? You put rocks on. They call them slingshots. We would just use those and kill birds and squirrels. Yes, it was really hard.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: There was one place where I am from that was a place for the sick. One time I visited them, there was an elder lady in that hospital. It was kind of snowy, and after a while a bird came and perched near the window. She said, “That is the kind I want.” “Sometimes, did y’all used to eat that kind?” I asked. “Yes, we would eat that kind,” she said.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That is what I was telling those growing up, that were sitting there. You probably would not want to eat the way we did. But also, as it is written in the Bible, it is going to happen again. It says famine may even be harder.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Amen, but we who believe and have been helped by Jesus Christ, we have called Him to help us. We will make it through good.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: It says not to be worried about what you are going to eat. In the Old Testament, it is written, “In the year that starvation happened, God fed those, and it came from above.” It was like it was hailing. Some preacher said that the Christians are going to die from starvation, and the way I see it is that God is going to feed them, for those who believe.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, He is going to get us through good. Yeah, we might not get what we want, but…

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: It is just like the things we want all the time. He is not going to give us the things we want. It’s what we need, what we really are in need of, He is going to give it to us. And that is when He said, “The trumpet is going to sound in the last days. Many people are going to scream,” it says, “that have not believed.” And that is when they do something to God’s people, when they mistreat them, He said to raise your heads and look up. Your help will be coming. He really is going to set us free. He is going to fail for as many people that do not want to believe. They that don’t want to are going to cry out, it says. Those who are laughing are going to cry, it says.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And when they don’t listen to the word, and hardly stand in Jesus Christ, that’s when they are going to kneel, it says.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Everyone on earth is going to kneel in His name, it says. Yeah, that is true.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I really believe we are near.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That is what it says. This must’ve been what Jesus was doing when He was here. When He was about to die and go home, He was telling them what was going to happen to Him, how He was going back to His Father. He was telling them, and now He is telling us. He is coming back, even if you don’t understand and believe. He is making it clear that He is coming back. I was saying that what is written is being fulfilled.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: If you really think about it, He is speaking to us kindly.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: But as time goes on…

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: When He comes back, He is not going to be friendly. He is going to get who belongs to Him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He is going to be the king. Man.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: I find it sometimes in the Old Testament, “If people on earth would come to me and believe,” He said, “I will not curse the world anymore.” He would excuse us if the world believed, but it will not happen. They would not believe.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Boy, there is a lot written in His Holy Word if you pay attention, if you really dig deep to what is written.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: I really find it interesting when I read.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: When y’all were growing up, you said a while ago y’all still lived there. Were there a lot of y’all that lived nearby?

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Y’all were related.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: There is a huge hollow there where we live, when our late father lived there. He had almost 500 acres. Almost all that hollow was his, and then, when he passed, it all went down.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: We still live there nowadays. All the family and relatives live there. It’s a little bit of a hollow, and that is where we live.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: It’s true, where we live, they call it Eagle Hollow. Where we live, that whole hollow they named Eagle Hollow.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Is it still called that? Eagle Hollow?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Yes, they have forgotten about a little bit. I made a sign and hung it on a metal pole at the turn-off. It says ‘Eagle Hollow’ is what is written. I thought, they really do forget. That is what they would say: Eagle Hollow Road. They would call it that. But it was slowing down, so I put up a sign for them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Is it as it was, or is there more of y’all now?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: No, there are fewer of us now. We lost three sisters. We have really decreased since our mother passed away. It was then that it started. We are alone, and this one is home alone where his mom used to live. He spends the days alone. I live with two boys. It’s just us. We never see anyone. We really are orphans. “Let’s love one another and help each other,” I was telling them there. Really, it’s just a few of us that live there now. There were six houses there when Dad was alive, that he built for people to live in. He would loan the houses out for free, and that is all gone nowadays.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: Nowadays, we are family that live there. There is nobody else. There is one, a white. He lives way out towards the woods, but that is it. The rest is just family. That church that is built there, they say it belongs to us. Our mother gave to them, the one they call Fellowship Church.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, OK.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: We live near there.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: The members say that it is our church. But we don’t hear the leaders there say anything like that. All we see is a big picture of our late mother for giving them the land.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: But your mother had given them the land, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: There was not any single person she chose to give it to. It was for all the community living there. Because we are family.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yes, it was good that she did that.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: She really did good.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: They have a white preacher.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: True, yeah?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That is what she said at the time she gave it to them. “My children and my grandchildren will have a place to go to church,” she thought, and that is what she said at the time she gave it to them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, she really did a joyful thing.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: It’s amazing. I don’t know if you have seen it. It really is a huge, good building. They really have it fixed up good.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I pastor at Steele sometimes. They say, there on a nearby ridge, there lived a certain person. Sometimes he would come when they were having church. “This is my building and also it is my say-so,” he would say. And also, when the pastor was preaching, he would again interfere, they said. Your mother really did good when you said she let it all go.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: As for me, I can see the good that has been done when we go there. That is all I see, and also I see how strong it is supposed to be. When we are there, nothing like that can be seen. And we don’t - what you said someone was doing [interfere]. Because someone is doing bad when they do that. You should be happy when there is a church on your property.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, but sometimes, what did happen, it might have been the children. They let it all go - a big area. They were given a big area with a creek running in the back at Steele. They were given all of that. But the creek flows, and some don’t want anyone in the water.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That’s true.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: But God has allowed that creek to flow.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: This land that she gave them also has a creek. It was a pretty good bend of a creek near the porch, but they fixed it. They made the water go toward the back. It doesn’t bother the church anymore. They dug a ditch toward the back and made the water go that way. Things are good now.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: My late mother’s aunt used to tell me to call her grandmother, and I really called her grandmother. She had a huge property where they call Bull Hollow. There was a creek there. I was just yea tall [gestures] when I would go there in the summer. When we were not in school, I would visit her. And also, she had some kettles way over there, two of them, and also the washers they had a long time ago. You could just go like that [gestures]. You could put it through just by doing that. She had that kind, and a chair sitting over there and a place to eat at, kind of a picnic table. She let people nearby come if they wanted to wash clothes. Sometimes, in the summer, early in the morning, there would already be smoke. Someone had come and had built a fire underneath the kettle, heating up the water. And then that one would wash. They would wash, and then sometimes someone would come and say, “Y’all come and eat.” And then we would agree and go eat the cooking. Then one day, when she was getting old, a white came and said, “I would like to buy this land from you,” and for a while, they talked about the price and different things they talked about. “Would you continue to provide a place that is prepared so they can wash?” she asked that white. “Yeah, yeah, I would let them. I would let them all the time,” he said. And so, the white bought it. The first year it was like it was, and then the second year he built a fence. Nobody could go there. It was not very long before the water that was flowing beautifully dried up.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: It was good in the past. We should have the key, if we want to cook and eat. For instance, an anniversary. There should be a place to go, if you think about it. I don’t know what it’s like where you are from, but where we are from, the Cherokee are hungry for the Cherokee message. They can’t find it. There are a few in that church. There are a few that he has given. There are just a few Cherokees in there, and those that are in there are hungry for the Cherokee message. They don’t go to a Cherokee service. A long time ago, where the native churches were in the woods, they were all Cherokee. I remember at Belfonte, there was not a chance you would see a white at a service. If there was, there would be a reason a white would be in there. He would be wanting something.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s true, that is the way it was. I remember when I was growing up, we went to church at Brush Creek. We would travel by foot, and now, nobody will go if they must walk.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Where we live, we would walk that far to Belfonte. To get there, we took a small road that went straight through the woods. We had a road.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And for us, they just had that coal oil kerosene for lights.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: In Belfonte, they had those glasses with kerosene in them, and they had cloths in them. They would shine them, and some would travel a long way.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And I also remember when a preacher would stand up, sometimes there it would be, sitting right there; he would do this [gestures] and read it in Cherokee, and then he would preach from there. While he was reading, it would be doing this [gestures]. When he would preach, he would preach that when it was hot, they would just raise the windows up.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That is the way it was at Belfonte. The chairs there had nails that were sticking out. Sitting down, I think I tore two or three pants that got hung up. There were plenty of elders that prayed that God had compassion for, and now they have cushions that are that thick laying there and everywhere. And another thing: the same as Noah was told to build a boat for him, he built a big boat for lots of people to enter. But not a lot of people entered. Only eight entered. I believe God still does the same thing. He is allowing huge places to have church, and still nobody is coming in, the same as they were not entering that boat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Over here where DJ pastors, you know where that’s at?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: On every fourth, they preach in all Cherokee and sing in all Cherokee. And I will be there tomorrow night to preach in Cherokee and to sing in Cherokee. This last time on the fourth, your pastor came there. He and I switch off. Tomorrow evening, I will be there.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That is what preachers did a long time ago, and they had messengers. They would go everywhere. Sometimes one went to Belfonte weekly. You don’t hear of that anymore. They would have church 10 nights sometimes. If they scheduled five, they would extend it. Nowadays, four nights is too long to have church, but I think about how there were all Cherokee members a long time ago. The preachers didn’t speak English. It was Cherokee. They didn’t have any English. That is why. One time, we were having church at Belfonte and we were all Cherokee. After a while, halfway through the preaching, someone came. A big man. We knew him - he was mean. He beat up police. He was mean and unpredictable. He came in, he sat in front and he was talking loudly. At the time, I didn’t go to church. I was sitting in the back. He was talking loudly during the preaching. He was interfering. The deacons knew him. They were afraid to say something to that man. He was interrupting him preaching. After a while, a deacon came and said, “Can you get him out of here?” I said, “I can get him out of here.” I was feeling a little bit afraid, because I knew him, but I told the deacon I could get him out of there. I walked slowly to where he was sitting. His name was Star. “Star,” I said, “Star, let’s go outside.” He said, “OK,” and he got up. I thought when we got outside, I was going to outrun him. When we got outside, he said, “I’m going to shake your hand. I am glad you got me out of there. I know I shouldn’t have been in there like this,” he told me. He appreciated that. They could have gotten him out that easy, but they were afraid of him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It has all really changed now, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Yeah, a lot.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: When your parents were alive, did they know some medicine that was in the woods, for instance, roots?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Yeah, they knew.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: My dad was a healer.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Healing by touching, that is what he did.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: He would heal children.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I’ll be.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: He knew a lot of medicine, too.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: “I know lots of mean things to do, but I am afraid of my God,” he said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s it.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: They would ask him for that, but he would refuse them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You probably know medicine from the woods.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: He doesn’t know anything. He didn’t learn anything.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: I knew some, but I have forgotten what kind I used. My late father would point out what kind it was. It was for the kidney, the last time we went, but that kind is hard to find.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Even that medicine that the Cherokee knew has gone away. It is going away a lot. God has really given the Cherokee medicine. They could not go to the doctor because of no money. Nobody would take them. They knew medicine and they knew how to use it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s true. I remember some of the elders who were alive knew the medicine you get from the woods.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: That is how my mother was. If there was a child yea tall [gestures] that had a fever, she would go look for plants. I went with her, but I was too little. She would go to the water that was about that deep [gestures], and that is where the plants were. They were easy to pull out. The root was white, and she would boil that for them. She would heal them. Mom knew pretty good medicine. Well, both. My dad, too, for treating cancer, I know that.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Guy, I’m going to ask you something. It has really been bothering me. I think about how people are learning witchcraft. Do you believe a preacher should learn that? That is what I think.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No way.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: It is written in the Bible. It says it belongs to Satan. When Marten was our pastor, he wanted that. There was someone from where you are from, or somewhere. He told me, “We spent two weeks writing some paper,” he told me. He would really tell me things when he was our pastor. He didn’t tell the others anything. When he told me that, I thought hard. “Why did he want that?” I was thinking, “and he is a preacher. It is written in the Bible,” I was thinking. Me too, I had an uncle and his wife living in Vian, Gore. He was bad about things like that. I wanted to know what he knew. I wanted to learn. Back then, I wasn’t in church yet. “Be here in the morning before the sun rises. If you can be here, we will go to the water. You can cross the water seven times, and when you cross the water seven times, it will be yours,” he said to me. I said, “Alright, I will be there,” I told him. And so, I was in a rush and got up and went. That one who was going to teach me was not home. Why? They said he was in Tahlequah somewhere, and when I saw him again, I said to him, “You really lied to me.” No, Mom warned me. She warned me, and now I see what is written in the Bible. I am glad that I didn’t learn it. It’s true.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: God was working.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He knew, God knew when He looked upon you that you would be speaking the message.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Yeah, I was thinking that far. Guy, I got extremely sick. Somewhere around 57 or 58 years ago, my youngest son wasn’t born yet - I think he is 58 years old - then, as far as I knew, I was going to die. You couldn’t describe the way I felt, and I was going to the doctor. They were taking X-rays starting from my head, but they were not finding anything. They were telling me nothing was wrong with me. As far as I know, I was sick. I hadn’t even thought about church or going into a church back then. I crawled around on the ground. I told them and called and pleaded, till water came out of my eyes. That is how hard I pleaded. I didn’t want the children to grow up without their father, I was thinking. I told them I really crawled around on the ground and called. It is also written that He does not hear the sinners. But if He sees a certain one who really means it, He might hear him. I know I was a sinner - I was doing everything. Then, when I crawled around till water came out of my eyes, I told them that He heard me and lifted me up. “Not just until the children grow, if you would heal me, but to be able to do whatever you want,” and I made a huge promise when I said that to Him. “Whatever you want me to do if you heal me,” I was saying. I crawled into the woods, and I began to slowly get better. That has been 58 years now. As far as I knew, I was going to die. I was sick. I am glad that my life was extended, and I tell them, “He has extended my life.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It is also written in the Old Testament, if someone had a sickness, it says, and they prayed, they were given 18 or 15 years to live. Like you said, God can do it. Like you said, if they really mean it in prayer, if it begins deep inside the heart. Like you said, I believe He is going to do it. We really do have a good God to help us.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That was a big promise I made when I surrendered and became a Christian, and He told me again, “If you remain like you are here, if you remain just like you are, you are not able to help lots of people. Lots of people are going to be in want. There will be nothing you can do for them,” I was told, “if you remain like you are.” I was told again, and then I thought, He wants something from me. In time, they made me a licensed preacher at Belfonte. Then, when I became a licensed preacher, Chuculate called. They wanted me to go over there. I didn’t know the reason. I thought they were wanting a revival, but they were looking for somebody to pastor them. So, I went there and preached. They didn’t make any sign about what they wanted when I went there, and I went home. “Did they like you?” “I guess, I don’t know,” I told them. After a while, they called me back again. Then they chose me to pastor them. They said, “We can just lay hands on him here,” they said. When Guy was ordaining me, there was one verse that I couldn’t get, and if I didn’t get that one, I didn’t pass. I couldn’t get it. I knew I had read it, but I couldn’t remember it. I was sitting there, and they were sitting there, and we prayed, and they said, “Come on, Levi, you know that,” and they prayed. And it was just like that light, to where it was written. When I read that, Lawrence jumped up and said, “He passed!” That is when I realized I was where I promised Him I would be. I thought then, God’s work is amazing. This is also written: “When the tempter comes, it has probably met you before.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, man. Gah-lee.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Oh, me too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It’s painful.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That is one thing a deacon said at Belfonte. I have never seen how they talk about the tempter that people talk about. I found where it says in the Bible if anyone says that he is lying it is written that he has already gone astray as it is written we are not to say that. I had three hard tests come to me. There was one that was drunk walking, as I was driving to church. He was coming towards me drunk like this [gestures]. He came up the hill, and we met. I couldn’t decide which way to go to avoid him, that way or this way. I guess he thought I was trying to hit him, because I was trying to miss him. When I got straight to him, he had a fifth of wine that he threw at the pickup I was driving, but it hit the window glass on the side. It didn’t break the big glass, but it really soaked me. I was wet all over. We were having a revival at church. I was heading there and Lawrence was preaching. “Boy, what am I going to do?” There wasn’t enough time for me to go change my clothes and come back. He splashed it all over me. “What am I going to do?” I was thinking, but I went on to where they were having church. The only room to sit was next to where Lawrence was sitting. That was where I sat. I was sitting next to him. The next day I asked him, “Lawrence, when I sat next to you, did you smell anything?” “I didn’t smell anything,” he said. And that’s how wet I was from the wine - he didn’t smell anything and he was sitting right there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you think he was going to be sitting there drunk?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: I thought he was going to be doing this. And another time, we were hauling gravel near Marble City. I stopped at the gate near the entrance. I got out, and there were some boys sitting over there. I knew one of them. We were friends. They were sitting in the shade, drinking, when I got out and opened the gate. My friend got up. “Oh, Levi, I haven’t seen you in a long time. We are friends,” he said. “You are going to get a drink from me.” I told him, “No, I’m not taking a drink from you. I have quit.” He was coming towards me, and he told me, “You are going to have a drink, or I’m going to splash it on you.” I told him, “You are going to splash it on me, because I’m not taking a drink.” He was coming closer, and a friend of his who was sitting there then got up and told him, “You are not going to do that,” and broke it up. He already had it like this [gestures], and was coming toward me to splash it on me. That is how a hard test comes to you sometimes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That is true, that is the way it is. For instance, your late parents looked for things that were in the woods, like blueberry.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Yeah, back then there was a lot and I think about that also. Nowadays, it has gone away. I guess we’re not using what has been provided for us since it has gone away. I believe there were a lot of blueberry, blackberry, and dewberry - all of the different things. There was a lot that existed. It grew anywhere for them to eat. That also probably helped keep us alive.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I guess y’all who lived nearby all found blueberry, blackberry, and mushrooms.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Mushrooms.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And poke salad.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: We were a group. When the blackberry was everywhere, some white would come to buy it. He would bring quarts. Then we picked it, and my God, we were selling what we were provided. That is why He took it away, I believe. We were selling what we had been provided. God has provided us with everything, without any need to survive and live and raise our children. That is what He provided, as it is written in the Old Testament. When He got tired of them, when sin got full, He took it away.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s true. If we look around now, absolutely in good shape. Sometimes I make an example of what is written in the Bible. It says, “like a hen that covers its chicks.” That is what God does to us. He covers things up so nothing bad comes to us, and He protects the things that He loves. Y’all mentioned our needs a while ago. He gives it to us. He gives us nothing short of our needs. That’s it.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: God provides us, He provides for His people and it includes other people.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Just like we are here, the good things that happen to us and those that are out there that do not believe. It includes them.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Yeah, it includes them and the way they think about is God did it for them when they were included, and He was doing it for us instead.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s it, but they don’t think that.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: They don’t think that far.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How much time is left?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Five minutes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I am going to ask you both, is the Cherokee language going to fade away? Is it going to stop?

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: I don’t think so.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Say, for instance, in 20 years, do you think the Cherokee language will continue as it is?

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: It could fade away in that amount of time. I saw it written somewhere in a newspaper at the hospital. It was written that in a few years, the Cherokee language will not be known.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: But it was just a white talking.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: But another thing, if someone forgets Cherokee it’s their own fault. It’s not anyone’s fault. If I think about it, I can’t talk Cherokee. Wherever there is a native office, they will have Cherokee places in there, and they will speak to you in English. It’s not supposed to be like that. The other day I was at the clinic with my daughter in Stilwell. There were two women sitting in front of me. They were full Cherokee, but nobody talked in Cherokee. It was all in English. It is their own fault they don’t speak Cherokee.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: They are worried that Cherokee is going away. I was telling them it is our fault. He saw our pastor Charlie, and he said he was speaking to him in English.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: He was in the office where it was. It was over. It was a long time ago that I knew him. I used to play ball everywhere. I knew his brothers. I went into the office they pointed me to, and when he got up, it was all in English. I said, “Hey, I know you speak in Cherokee.”

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: They say we have just borrowed the English we speak. Cherokee is what we have been truly given.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: God has given us Cherokee.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: That is what I tell them. God has provided us with the Cherokee language. I told them if it wasn’t for that we would be mute. It’s true.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s true.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: But it is helpful that we can speak both.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, both.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: That is what I was telling the preachers. They speak both Cherokee and English and would prefer to preach in English. It should be both. It’s true at every church, the message should be put in both English and Cherokee.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: And another thing is what I’m talking about. Even if a Cherokee speaks to you in English, he will never become a white. He is always going to be brown.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: As for me, if I know that someone speaks Cherokee, I speak to them in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: I was telling my daughter that I do not like a Cherokee talking to me in English. We will talk a little while in English, and then I will just move away, I was telling her. They themselves are Cherokee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I will start first and say, “Hi, how are you?” “Yeah, I’m doing good,” he would say. “Don’t you speak Cherokee?” “No, I don’t understand,” he would say.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: That is what they will say to you.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: It’s a little bit like they are embarrassed to speak Cherokee. The Mexicans will holler around, talking.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They will be singing; the Mexicans will almost be like singing. Yeah.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: Our late mother didn’t hardly speak English good, but our late father spoke pretty good. That is just the way it was.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I appreciate this conversation we had.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: Me too. That was the hope that I had, that Guy would talk to us, I was thinking. He would be kind.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You wouldn’t fight.

segments.speaker: john-soap
segments.translation: If it was Charlie who talks to us, we are going to have to speak in English, I told him. I said I wasn’t.

segments.speaker: levi-eagle
segments.translation: I got to Sallisaw bank the other day. Omit if not in audio or delete from audio
